title: Ice-age crustal rebound as the cause of pole shift
place_text: North America, Hudson Bay, northwestern Europe

tellings.quote: I think that what happens is is that with the process of glaciation, rapid glaciation or rapid deglaciation, it induces a tremendous amount of instability in the Earth's crust that could manifest as an accelerated episode of continental of of lithospheric movement.

plain: A pole shift is the idea that Earth's outer shell can slide, moving lands to new places relative to the poles, a notion linked to the writer Charles Hapgood. Randall Carlson, a researcher, says that during the last great ice age and its melting, over places like North America, Hudson Bay and northwestern Europe, the rapid piling up and loss of ice could make the crust unstable enough to move faster than usual. If true, the planet's surface could shift suddenly enough to reshape the world humans lived in.
